experiment: Newton pendulum comparison (Principia, Book III, Prop. VI)
bodies: gold, silver, lead, glass, sand, common salt, wood, water, wheat (each vs wood; 11-ft pendulums)
quantity_as_published: fractional difference in quantity of matter at equal weight (sensitivity statement)
quote: By these experiments, in bodies of the same weight, I could manifestly have discovered a difference of matter less than the thousandth part of the whole, had any such been.
location: Book III, Proposition VI, Theorem VI (Motte 1729 English translation)
reference: Newton I. 1687, Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica, Book III Prop. VI; Engl. transl. A. Motte 1729 (Wikisource transcription)
notes: Primary text (Motte translation of the 3rd ed.) read on Wikisource. Same 1/1000 quoted by Eotvos, Pekar & Fekete 1922 p.15 ('kappa kleiner als 1/1000') and by the 1909 Goettingen prize report. It is an estimated sensitivity, not a statistical limit.

experiment: Bessel pendulums (length of the seconds pendulum for different substances, Koenigsberg)
bodies: gold, silver, lead, iron, zinc, brass, marble, clay, quartz, water, meteoric iron, meteoric stone (earlier runs: brass and ivory spheres)
quantity_as_published: largest fractional difference in seconds-pendulum length (= in g) between substances
quote: denn es findet sich nirgends ein Unterschied, welcher den sechszigtausendsten Theil des Ganzen betrüge, und welcher nicht den unvermeidlichen Fehlern der Versuche zugeschrieben werden könnte
reference: Bessel F. W. 1832, 'Versuche über die Kraft, mit welcher die Erde Körper von verschiedener Beschaffenheit anzieht', Annalen der Physik und Chemie 101 (2nd ser. vol. 25), 401-417 (reprinted from Astron. Nachr. 10, 97)
notes: 'no difference amounting to one sixty-thousandth of the whole' = 1/60000 = 1.67e-5; the usual '2e-5' (Tino et al. 2020; Will/TEGP tradition) is this rounded. Page image of the archive.org scan checked. EPF 1922 p.15 also gives Bessel as 1/60000. Potter (1923, p.588) adds that Bessel's water result was a possible exception. Astron. Nachr. version: doi 10.1002/asna.18330100701.

experiment: Eotvos torsion balance, first series (measured 1889; Earth's field, Earth-rotation centrifugal acceleration as reference)
bodies: brass vs glass, antimonite (stibnite) and cork; brass vs air (<1e-5)
quantity_as_published: fractional difference of weight per unit mass between materials (upper bound)
quote: úgy ez a különbség sárgaréz, üveg, antimonit és parafára vonatkozólag egy húsz milliomodnál, sárgaréz és levegőre vonatkozólag pedig egy százezrednél bizonyára kisebb.
reference: Eötvös R. 1890, 'A Föld vonzása különböző anyagokra', Akadémiai Értesítő 1, 108-110 (German version: Math. Naturwiss. Ber. Ungarn 8, 65)
notes: Translation: '...this difference for brass, glass, antimonite and cork is certainly smaller than one twenty-millionth, and for brass and air smaller than one hundred-thousandth.' Same page: 'more than 400 times more precise than Bessel'. 1/20 000 000 = 5e-8; the same number is quoted by EPF 1922 p.15 and the 1909 Goettingen report. Hungarian original read from the MTA REAL scan (page image checked).

experiment: Eotvos, Pekar & Fekete torsion balances (Goettingen Beneke-prize work; Earth's field)
bodies: platinum vs magnalium, snakewood, copper, water, crystalline CuSO4, CuSO4 solution, asbestos, tallow
quantity_as_published: kappa (specific attraction coefficient, f'=f(1+kappa)) differences kappa-kappa_Pt, Earth attraction; overall upper bound
quote: Wir glauben behaupten zu dürfen, daß bezüglich der Erdanziehung κ für all diese Körper den Wert von 0,005·10^-6 nicht erreicht.
location: p. 65 (summary table of kappa-kappa_Pt and conclusion)
reference: Eötvös R. v., Pekár D., Fekete E. 1922, Annalen der Physik (4) 68 (= vol. 373), 11-66
notes: Draft asked 3e-9 or 5e-9: the paper states 0.005e-6 = 5e-9 (results are in units of 10^-6). Individual results (kappa-kappa_Pt, +/- 'mittlerer Fehler' = standard error) range from +0.004+/-0.001 (magnalium) to -0.006+/-0.003 (water) x10^-6, i.e. errors 1-3e-9; full table in wep_notes.md. Sun (meridian) series: kappa_Magnalium-kappa_Pt = +0.006e-6 (no error). Measurements 1906-1908 (meridian series ran to Aug 1908); prize 1909 (Goettingen report quotes 1/200 000 000); paper published posthumously 1922. Will 2014 Fig. 1 plots about 5e-9. Secondary sources quote 3e-9 (Braginsky & Panov 1972; Tino et al. 2020) or 1e-8 (Peebles 2016; Nobili & Anselmi 2018; Eotvos' own 1909 London report per Bod et al. 1991). Page images of the scan checked.

experiment: Renner torsion balance (Budapest; repeat of Eotvos method with six azimuths)
bodies: paraffin, NH4F, Bi, Pt, glass, Mn-Cu alloy vs brass or Cu (pairs as listed by Bod et al. 1991)
quantity_as_published: claimed accuracy of material-independence of the gravitational constant (kappa)
quote: Die Gravitationskonstante ist für die untersuchten Stoffe allgemein bis zur Genauigkeit von 1 : 2 000 000 000, in einem Falle sogar von 1 : 5 000 000 000 von der Beschaffenheit der Körper unabhängig.
location: Renner's German abstract (Hungarian Academy session of 18 March 1935), reprinted verbatim in Bod et al. 1991, Appendix II
reference: Renner J. 1935, Matematikai és Természettudományi Értesítő 53, 542 (Hungarian, German abstract); abstract reprinted in Bod L., Fischbach E., Marx G., Náray-Ziegler M. 1991, Acta Phys. Hung. 69, 335
notes: Draft '~2e-9' is NOT Renner's own claim: he claimed 1:2e9 = 5e-10 generally (2e-10 in one case), with mean ('mittlere') errors averaging +/-0.52e-9 and every difference below its mean error. Roll, Krotkov & Dicke 1964 showed his time-interpolated readings were not independent, so errors were underestimated by ~x3 (Kiraly: x2.4) and his results lie 'suspiciously near zero' (Bod et al. 1991); x3 gives ~1.6e-9, hence the ~1-2e-9 seen in reviews (Will 2014 Fig. 1 plots about 1.3e-9). Journal itself not reachable: the quote is Renner's own abstract as reprinted; Bod et al. print the volume as 13 (likely a typo for 53).

experiment: Princeton torsion balance (Roll, Krotkov & Dicke; Sun as attractor, 24-h modulation)
quote: the various measurements of η, obtained from the gravitational acceleration toward the sun, gave a substantially Gaussian distribution with mean value η(Au, Al) = (1.3 ± 1.0) × 10^−11. The probable error quoted for the mean is based upon the observed scatter in results from individual data runs, assuming a Gaussian distribution.
reference: Roll P. G., Krotkov R., Dicke R. H. 1964, Annals of Physics 26, 442-517
notes: Abstract (Elsevier text via INSPIRE record 9227) also says: 'enable us to conclude with 95% confidence that |η(Au, Al)| < 3 × 10^−11'. Although the abstract calls +/-1.0 a 'probable error', it behaves like a 1-sigma standard error: with sigma=1.0 the probability that |eta|<3e-11 is 95.5%, matching the 95% statement; a true probable error (sigma=1.48) would give a 95% bound of about 3.8e-11. Braginsky & Panov 1972 quote RKD as '<3e-11 with 95% confidence'. Full text (Elsevier) not accessible. Data taken c. 1959-1963.

experiment: Moscow torsion balance (Braginsky & Panov; Sun as attractor; 8-mass star-shaped balance)
quote: An experiment is described which establishes with 0.9 x 10^-12 accuracy (95% confidence) that the ratio of the inertial to the gravitational mass is identical for aluminum and platinum.
location: abstract; result (-0.3 ± 0.9)×10^-12 'with 95% confidence' in Eq. (6), p. 465
reference: Braginskii V. B., Panov V. I. 1972, Sov. Phys. JETP 34, 463-466 [Zh. Eksp. Teor. Fiz. 61, 873-879 (1971)]
notes: Draft '<9e-13 (which CL?)': it is 95% confidence, and the measured value is (-0.3 +/- 0.9)e-12 (Eq. 6, 'Our result ... = (-0.3 ± 0.9)×10^-12'). The 95% interval is a Student-t interval from 7 film records (Feb 1971); with t(6 dof)=2.45 the 1-sigma equivalent would be about 0.37e-12 (my inference). Russian original 1971, English translation 1972; measurements Feb 1971. PDF from the JETP archive (jetp.ras.ru).
